title: How many bounces before it stops? More than the counter shows. 80%: at rest by 4.06 s, 90%: 8.58 s
description:
How many bounces before it stops? A ball is dropped from 1 m onto a hard floor with no air (g = 9.80665 m/s^2), once keeping 80 percent of its speed on every bounce (coefficient of restitution 0.8, so 64 percent of its height) and once keeping 90 percent (0.9, 81 percent of its height). Two panels, the same drop, released at the same instant and drawn at the same scale. The flights are event-driven with closed forms: the drop takes t0 = sqrt(2 h / g), bounce n leaves the floor at 0.8^n (or 0.9^n) times the impact speed, rises to h times 0.8^(2n) and flies for 2 t0 times 0.8^n; the sim counts bounces down to a stated floor, the first bounce under 0.001 mm, and freezes the counter there. The first flights are checked by an RK4 free-flight integration at 6,000 steps per second with floor-crossing interpolation. The ball is a point for every number and is drawn larger than life. Played at 1/4 speed with the clocks in real seconds; deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- the drop takes 0.4516 s and lands at 4.4287 m/s
- 80 percent: bounce 1 rises to 0.640 m and lasts 0.7226 s; 15 bounces rise above 1 mm; bounce 16 is the first under 1 mm (0.79 mm, 25 ms long, leaving the floor at 3.937 s); bounce 31 is the first under 0.001 mm (0.00098 mm, leaving the floor at 4.0599 s); closed-form stop time t0 (1 + 0.8) / (1 - 0.8) = 9 t0 = 4.0644 s; path length h (1 + 0.64) / (1 - 0.64) = 4.5556 m (4.555552 m summed to bounce 31)
- 90 percent: bounce 1 rises to 0.810 m and lasts 0.8129 s; 32 bounces rise above 1 mm; bounce 33 is the first under 1 mm (0.96 mm, 28 ms long, leaving the floor at 8.301 s); bounce 66 is the first under 0.001 mm (0.00091 mm, leaving the floor at 8.5718 s); stop time 19 t0 = 8.5804 s; path length 9.5263 m (9.526308 m summed to bounce 66)
- the 90 percent ball takes 2.111 times as long to lie at rest
- no bounce height is zero: bounce 32 of the 80 percent ball would rise to 6.3e-7 m and bounce 100 to 4e-20 m; the counters stop only at the stated floor
- RK4 check over the drop and the first five bounces: landing times within 2.6e-7 s, landing speeds within 4.9e-7 m/s and bounce heights within 9e-8 m of the closed forms

Why: each bounce keeps a fixed fraction of the speed, and a flight lasts as long as its launch speed, so each flight lasts 0.8 (or 0.9) times the one before. The flight times are one number multiplied by 0.8 again and again: a geometric series. That list has no last term, because 0.8 times something positive is always positive, so the counter never finds a last bounce. But the terms shrink so fast that they add up to a fixed total: the first flight divided by (1 - 0.8), five times the first flight. Add the drop and every bounce of the 80 percent ball is over by 9 t0 = 4.064 s; for 0.9 the factor is 1 / (1 - 0.9) = 10, and everything is over by 19 t0 = 8.580 s. The heights add up the same way to 4.56 m and 9.53 m of path. That is Zeno's paradox in a bouncing ball: more steps than any counter can show, all finished before a fixed moment. A real ball stops sooner, because the last bounces are smaller than the ball's own squash and the floor's roughness, and the clatter blurs into a buzz; but its total time is still bounded by this sum.

Rerun sims/zenobounce/zenobounce.py with projects/zenobounce/manifest.json and you get these numbers exactly.
